title: Europe's power sector hits 80% zero-carbon generation by 2030, but misses its own renewables target
gist: Wood Mackenzie's Europe Power Markets Strategic Planning Outlook 2026 projects Europe's power mix surpassing 80% zero-carbon by 2030 and demand rising 66% by 2050, yet the EU27 renewables share (63.7%) misses Fit-for-55 and REPowerEU targets; offshore wind delays keep gas generation 6% above prior forecasts while batteries more than triple by 2030.

insights.claim: Wood Mackenzie projects total European power demand across 35 markets reaching 4,103 TWh by 2030, 11% above 2025, and 6,152 TWh by 2050, a 66% increase.
insights.speaker: Wood Mackenzie
insights.so_what: Multi-decade load growth underpins long-run European grid and generation investment.
insights.quote: Total power demand reaches 4,103 TWh by 2030, 11% above 2025 levels, before climbing to 6,152 TWh by 2050, a 66% increase.

insights.claim: Data centres are the primary near-term driver of European power demand, while from the 2030s falling electricity prices shift electrification economics and trigger a new growth wave.
insights.speaker: Wood Mackenzie
insights.so_what: Near-term demand is AI/data-centre led; later growth depends on cheap power enabling electrification.
insights.quote: Near term, data centres are the primary driver.

insights.claim: European EV electricity consumption is projected to grow 15-fold from 39 TWh in 2025 to 577 TWh by 2050, underpinned by bans on new internal combustion vehicle sales.
insights.speaker: Wood Mackenzie
insights.so_what: EV charging becomes a major load source, supporting grid and charging infrastructure.

insights.claim: On-grid hydrogen in Europe scales from near zero in 2025 to 417 TWh by 2050.
insights.speaker: Wood Mackenzie
insights.so_what: Hydrogen electrolysis is projected as a material future power load.

insights.claim: Heat pump demand expands more than fivefold by 2060, but high upfront costs and unfavourable electricity-to-gas price ratios mean most markets fall short of national targets.
insights.speaker: Wood Mackenzie
insights.so_what: Heat pump adoption is price-ratio constrained, tempering growth for heat pump makers.

insights.claim: Northern Europe records the strongest demand growth at 81% by 2050 while Southern Europe trails at 52%.
insights.speaker: Wood Mackenzie
insights.so_what: Regional demand divergence guides where to deploy capital.

insights.claim: Wood Mackenzie's demand forecast is about 2% lower than its previous outlook as heat and hydrogen electrification lag, with two-sided risk from geopolitics and commodity prices versus prolonged fossil fuel disruption accelerating electrification.
insights.speaker: Wood Mackenzie
insights.so_what: Downward revision flags slower electrification, but fossil disruption is an upside catalyst.

insights.claim: Europe's zero-carbon power share exceeds 80% by 2030 and reaches 93% by 2050.
insights.speaker: Wood Mackenzie
insights.so_what: Near-total decarbonisation of European power erodes long-run fossil generation value.

insights.claim: The EU27 renewables share of generation in 2030 is projected at 63.7%, below both the Fit-for-55 target of 65% and the REPowerEU goal of 69%.
insights.speaker: Wood Mackenzie
insights.so_what: Target shortfall could prompt further policy support or procurement acceleration.
insights.quote: On an EU27 basis, the 2030 share stands at 63.7%, below both the Fit-for-55 target of 65% and the REPowerEU goal of 69%.

insights.claim: Solar PV capacity nearly doubles to 637 GWac by 2030, adding around 61 GW per year, while onshore wind adds 17 GW per year to reach 346 GW.
insights.speaker: Wood Mackenzie
insights.so_what: Sustained solar and onshore wind build supports equipment and developer volumes.

insights.claim: European offshore wind grows to 73 GW by 2030 and 148 GW by 2035, but supply chain pressures and investor uncertainty have delayed its trajectory.
insights.speaker: Wood Mackenzie
insights.so_what: Offshore wind delays are a persistent risk for developers and turbine suppliers.

insights.claim: Renewables reach 65% of supply across 35 European markets by 2030 and 83% by 2050.
insights.speaker: Wood Mackenzie
insights.so_what: Rising renewables share pressures capture prices and boosts flexibility value.

insights.claim: European battery storage more than triples from 47 GW to 163 GW by 2030, one of the largest near-term capital deployment opportunities in the European energy sector.
insights.speaker: Wood Mackenzie
insights.so_what: Battery storage is a leading near-term European investment theme.
insights.quote: one of the largest near-term capital deployment opportunities in the European energy sector

insights.claim: Germany, the UK, Italy and Poland account for over half of Europe's battery storage growth to 2030.
insights.speaker: Wood Mackenzie
insights.so_what: Storage capital should concentrate in these four markets.

insights.claim: Load growth from the second half of the 2030s will provide day-ahead price support, relieving renewable owners facing low capture prices as solar expands, while curtailment risks rise where grid lags capacity.
insights.speaker: Wood Mackenzie
insights.so_what: Renewable merchant economics may improve after 2035 but near-term capture-price and curtailment risk persists.

insights.claim: Natural gas generation in Europe averages 6% higher in 2026-2040 than Wood Mackenzie's prior forecast because offshore wind downgrades created a supply gap that gas filled.
insights.speaker: Wood Mackenzie
insights.so_what: Offshore wind delays extend gas burn and support gas-fired asset values near term.
insights.quote: offshore wind downgrades created a supply gap and gas filled it
insights.locator: Gas runs higher than the previous

insights.claim: European gas capacity rises 5% to 273 GW by 2030 even as fleet utilisation falls from 27% to 22%, with capacity mechanisms and flexibility revenues central to the investment case.
insights.speaker: Wood Mackenzie
insights.so_what: Gas plant value shifts from energy volume to capacity and flexibility payments.
insights.quote: Gas is retained for flexibility rather than volume
insights.locator: Gas runs higher than the previous

insights.claim: Gas volumes converge with the previous outlook by the mid-2040s and power supply from gas declines 45% by 2060.
insights.speaker: Wood Mackenzie
insights.so_what: Long-run gas generation decline caps terminal value of gas assets.

insights.claim: Mohammed Alraood says gas remains in Europe's mix not for volume but for the moments renewables cannot deliver.
insights.speaker: Mohammed Alraood
insights.so_what: Peaker and flexible gas business models gain relevance.
insights.quote: Gas remains in the mix, not for volume but for the moments renewables cannot deliver.

insights.claim: European coal generation halves from 457 TWh in 2025 to 237 TWh by 2030, and the EU27 coal fleet exits the mix by 2050.
insights.speaker: Wood Mackenzie
insights.so_what: Rapid coal decline removes demand for thermal coal in European power.

insights.claim: Nuclear is gaining ground in Europe via life extensions, new-build programmes and policy reversals in Switzerland and Serbia.
insights.speaker: Wood Mackenzie
insights.so_what: Nuclear policy reversals widen opportunities in nuclear supply chain.

insights.claim: Mohammed Alraood argues rising emissions costs will force structural decisions that markets are only beginning to price in.
insights.speaker: Mohammed Alraood
insights.so_what: Carbon cost repricing may not yet be fully reflected in asset valuations.
insights.quote: Rising emissions costs will force structural decisions that markets are only beginning to price in.

insights.claim: For European power developers and investors, the critical variable is which markets combine policy certainty, grid capacity and genuine load growth to make projects financeable.
insights.speaker: Mohammed Alraood
insights.so_what: Three-factor screen for market selection: policy certainty, grid capacity, load growth.
insights.quote: It is which markets combine policy certainty, grid capacity and genuine load growth to make projects financeable.

insights.claim: Whether Europe's transition delivers on time depends on grid investment and interconnector expansion, variables no forecast can fully determine.
insights.speaker: Wood Mackenzie
insights.so_what: Grid and interconnector buildout is the key bottleneck and investment theme.
